items.title: Adopt the repo rulebook (doc 18)
items.unblocks: the whole anti-drift system becoming law
items.detail: This is the rulebook born from your phone idea, designed properly with you in the remote session, and battle-tested by tonight's cleanup. Adopting it makes four habits law for every session in every repo: (1) THE LOGBOOK - one shared file in the planning repo where every pack handover, request between repos, and incident gets one line, so repos stop depending on someone remembering; (2) THE PASSPORT - no pack enters a repo without a small where-I-came-from slip (source, version, fingerprint), and importers refuse packs without one; (3) THE SESSION RECIPE - page 1 answers 'which repo do I open', including the janitor rules we used tonight (safety tags first, tests before pushes, you click anything destructive); (4) THE HANDOFF HOOK - every session-end handoff asks 'do I owe the logbook a line'. Adopting changes how sessions work going forward; it does not rebuild anything existing.

items.title: Pack tools refuse to export unsaved/unpushed work
items.unblocks: never again losing a pack's recipe
items.detail: Every pack-making tool (tiles, worlds, world-filler, sprites, audio) gets one safety check: it refuses to export a pack while its own code has unsaved changes or commits that exist only on this machine. This is exactly what nearly made the game's character art unrebuildable - the art pack came from tool code no branch on GitHub contained. Tonight's cleanup found the same pattern again in a smaller way (a half-merged main that was never pushed). YES means each tool repo gets a small paste-ask to add the check in its own lane; the tools' behavior is otherwise untouched.

items.detail: Your call from the forklift session: zones keep a general level progression, but deliberately contain cross-band pockets — an endgame corner inside a starter zone (walk in, get one-shot, learn and remember), a high-level dungeon under a low-level city. Your words: 'we can potentially score a lot here.' This card asks: is this a named pillar (protected, always considered in zone work) or just a normal rule?

items.title: Name it a pillar: everything in the world has a reason a villager could tell you
items.unblocks: world_filler direction sessions, all placement work
items.detail: Your call: the world must never feel like objectives placed on a map. Every camp, dungeon, rare route, and road has an in-world reason discoverable by looking at it. Working test for any placement: 'what is this doing here?' should have an answer a villager could give. Wolves denning above the sheep farms passes; 'a level-8 camp because this is the level-8 area' fails. (Extra timely: the mob/boss placement rehearsal is running RIGHT NOW — this pillar is its judging test.)

items.title: Night and weather may never make the game harder to see or heavier to run
items.detail: Your recorded pet peeve turned into a standing guardrail: whenever day/night or weather get built (both deferred), night must never be a visibility tax that makes grinding feel bad, and weather must never cost framerate. Atmosphere only ever adds. Adopting this now means no future session can build a darkness-tax night by default.

items.title: Adopt the aliveness test: organic enemies first, loot worth reading second, sound you never mute third
items.detail: Your own definition from today, in order: (1) enemies and camps read as organic places, not generic placements — the prerequisite for caring at all; (2) drops that make you stop and read the stats; (3) music and sfx good enough that you don't mute them (already passed — you historically mute game music and haven't muted this). 'When I want to play the game, that is when it feels alive.' This orders the first-slice work.

items.title: Testers move behind the loop - Gate 1 rewritten
items.unblocks: the go-hard phase starting without a doomed recruitment drive
items.detail: Already ruled by you in-session tonight (2026-07-30, ~04:20) - this click is the rested ratification. The old plan's Gate 1 wanted fresh outside testers judging the combat lab: 10-16 recruited candidates, at least 4 strangers per cycle. Your ruling: that is not realistic for a game at this shape in 2026. Strangers try an early build once and never twice, which means fresh eyes are spent the moment they touch it - they are the one resource you cannot renew. A failed recruitment drive produces silence, and silence always reads as 'the game is bad' when it really means 'nobody saw it'. It was also the only gate in the whole project that depended on other people's behavior instead of your own effort. So: (1) cold recruitment is RETIRED, not postponed - no public tester channel until the game can attract players on its own; (2) the go-hard phase builds THE LOOP first - the pieces already exist (world, town, bosses, sprites, audio), what is missing is the playable run that uses them; (3) human judgment returns as 2-3 warm, WATCHED first looks once the loop bar (next card) is met. The old rule's heart - 'the gate is never judged solely by the builder' - survives; it just waits until there is a game for someone to judge. This reverses the outside-tester rule from 2026-07-26 with cause: that rule assumed recruitable strangers, and the assumption fails against reality. The tester-build pipeline itself stays - tonight's clean 58.7 MB zip is exactly what will make the warm looks effortless.
options: Roll it back - keep the old Gate 1

items.title: The loop bar - what earns the first fresh look (make it yours)
items.unblocks: a finish line for the go-hard phase so it cannot recede forever
items.detail: The draft bar, written to be rewritten in YOUR words - this is the target the go-hard phase aims at, so it has to be yours. Draft: a person can sit down unguided and get one complete run - spawn in the town, walk out, fight through rising danger where loot actually drops and matters, reach the first boss or die trying, death costs something real, and dying makes you want to press retry NOW. When that run exists and stays fun for YOU playing it every day for a week straight, the 2-3 warm watched testers get called for their one fresh look. Two honest notes baked in: the bar is about FEEL and STAKES, not polish - your genre forgives dated visuals and never forgives flat combat; and from now on test scenes should be built so they leave playable content behind where possible, so testing accretes into the game instead of leaving scaffolding (your own observation tonight: the batteries verified every system, but 'playable' was never a gated artifact - this card makes it one).
options: I will rewrite the bar in my words

items.title: Death in normal mode: run back + gold cost
items.unblocks: the loop's stakes without forcing hardcore on anyone
items.detail: Already ruled by you in the loop design conversation (2026-07-30) - this click is the rested ratification. Dying WITHOUT permadeath on: you respawn in town, lose a slice of your gold (exact percentage tuned later), and the walk back to where you were is part of the price - dying deep costs real time. Your equipment is never taken in normal mode. Permadeath stays a choice made when creating a character: people who pick it want that experience, people who skip it get real-but-fair stakes. Hardcore death = the character is gone.

items.title: The loot frame: five tiers + boss-tied uniques
items.unblocks: loot that moves you forward AND gives you something to chase
items.detail: Already ruled by you (2026-07-30) - this click is the rested ratification. Equipment comes in five tiers, T1 to T5, dropping mainly from normal enemies (bosses can drop it too). Unique items only come from bosses; each unique is tied to its specific boss so you can grind AIMED at the item you want, and one boss can hold several uniques in his table. Rates demand real effort but stay reachable; no pity system - the breadth of other rewards is the consolation on dry streaks, exactly as the design document already binds. Tiers are how you progress through the world; uniques are the goal you chase.

items.title: Levels and XP are part of the loop
items.unblocks: the zero-to-hero feel arriving with the first loop
items.detail: Already ruled by you (2026-07-30) - this click is the rested ratification. The plan always had levels and XP, so the first loop includes them in minimal form: enemies grant XP, levels arrive on a simple curve, stats grow in small honest steps. Class skill trees wait for later - this is just the feeling of getting stronger while you hunt gear.

items.title: First boss: Bone Reliquary King wearing the proven kit
items.unblocks: a real boss at the loop's edge without weeks of new boss work
items.detail: Already ruled by you (2026-07-30) - this click is the rested ratification. The three-phase elite that is already built, tuned, and bot-proven dodgeable gets the Bone Reliquary King's look from your 13-boss pack (the name can change down the road). He guards the far edge of the danger gradient and carries the loop's first unique drop, per your named-challenge rule. A brand-new bespoke boss kit comes later - this gets a real boss into the loop now.
